summary: This program stores the whole number 42 in a variable and prints it to the screen. It shows that println can display numbers, not just text in quotes.

lines.text: Every Java program lives inside a class, and the class name must match the file name, so this code belongs in PrintNumber.java.
This is the method Java runs first when the program starts; all the work happens inside its braces.
The keyword int declares a variable that holds whole numbers, and the value 42 is stored in it under the name number.
Passing the variable without quotation marks prints the value it holds; writing "number" instead would print the word itself.
